correctness.rationale: For compact planar convex K of area A with strictly interior anchor z, the continuous positive bounded radial function ρ has A=(1/2)∫ρ². Conditioning on X−z=r eθ, the Y−z strip |det|<t has first-order area 2t[ρ(θ)+ρ(θ+pi)]/r. Its upper bound 2t diam(K)/r cancels the polar density r dr dθ and permits dominated convergence at r=0. Integrating yields slope 2H/A for D=|det|/A, H=2A+I, I=∫ρ(θ)ρ(θ+pi), equivalently 8−(1/A)∫(ρ−ρ_pi)². Strict 4<C<=8 follows from 0<I<=2A; equality at 8 iff ρ=ρ_pi continuously, so K centrally symmetric about z. As z approaches any boundary point, antipodal radial-product integral tends to zero by a supporting line and dominated convergence; lower bound 4 is sharp. Affine invariance uses equal scaling of det and area. For the marked law, φ=θ+b pi+σ arcsin(A eps q/(rs)) has Jacobian A eps/[rs sqrt(1−(A eps q/(rs))²)]; cancellation against polar rs density gives a pointwise limiting conditional density 1/(2H) on the two radial intervals, 0<q<1 and two equally likely signs. Both densities integrate to one, so Scheffé gives total-variation convergence and the claimed branch probabilities/uniform radial marks. Own independent analytic oval check ρ=1+a cosθ at a=0,.2,.4 reproduced slope 8−4a²/(1+a²/2) and parallel probability 1/2+a²/4. The checked finite simulation source supports rather than proves the asymptotic.
